title: Derived pullback along an isomorphism of schemes is an equivalence of ambient derived categories
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$,
uniformizer $\varpi_E$, an integer $n\geq1$, and put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be an isomorphism of
schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and let
$D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ be the derived categories of
sheaves of $A$-modules on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].
Then the derived pullback
$Lg^*=L(g_n)^*:D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)\to D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] is an equivalence of categories: it is fully
faithful and essentially surjective. (A quasi-inverse is the functor induced by the
direct image $g_*$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] applied termwise, which is
$L(g^{-1})^*$.)

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(A_Y)$ and $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Mod}(A_X)$, the categories of module sheaves of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The small-skeleton and universe conventions in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] ensure that these categories are abelian. Write $F=g^{-1}:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and $G=g_*:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$. Parts (2) and (3) of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] give an exact equivalence on these module categories, with coefficients identified through the specified isomorphism $c^g_A$. More explicitly, extension of scalars in the module pullback of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] along $c^g_A$ is naturally isomorphic to the identity after identifying the rings: $m\otimes a\mapsto am$, with inverse $m\mapsto m\otimes1$. Thus the module pullback is $F$. Choose adjoint-equivalence data for the equivalence in part (2), with unit $\eta:\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal A}\xrightarrow{\sim}GF$ and counit $\varepsilon:FG\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal B}$, satisfying the triangle identities. The functor $G$ is exact as well: an equivalence carries the universal diagrams for kernels and cokernels to the corresponding universal diagrams, and its inverse does the same. Both functors are additive because they act on the underlying sheaves of abelian groups and on module homomorphisms.

proof.text: Let $Q_Y,Q_X$ be the derived localizations of cochain complexes of $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to both exact functors in step 1. This gives $F_D:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ and $G_D:D(\mathcal B)\to D(\mathcal A)$, with natural isomorphisms $F_DQ_Y\cong Q_XC(F)$ and $G_DQ_X\cong Q_YC(G)$; $C(F),C(G)$ denote termwise application. Both termwise functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms, with no boundedness assumption. The finite-level clause of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] identifies the specified $Lg^*$ with $F_D$: the derived pullback is inverse image applied termwise to every representative. On morphisms this is the same identification, since the factorization is a natural isomorphism of functors, and the uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] makes the identification independent of the factorization choices.

proof.text:
Apply $\eta$ and $\varepsilon$ in each degree of a complex. Naturality with respect to its differentials makes these chain isomorphisms $\eta^C:\mathrm{id}\xrightarrow{\sim}C(G)C(F)$ and $\varepsilon^C:C(F)C(G)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$. Their triangle identities hold degree by degree, using the triangle identities of the equivalence data in step 1, obtained from [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image](2). Write $p_K:F_DQ_YK\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_XC(F)K$ and $q_L:G_DQ_XL\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_YC(G)L$ for the factorization isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Put $a_K=q_{C(F)K}\circ G_D(p_K)$ and $b_L=p_{C(G)L}\circ F_D(q_L)$, so that $a_K:G_DF_DQ_YK\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_YC(G)C(F)K$ and $b_L:F_DG_DQ_XL\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_XC(F)C(G)L$. Part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] lifts the natural isomorphisms to $\eta^D:\mathrm{id}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_DF_D$ and $\varepsilon^D:F_DG_D\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$ with components $\eta^D_{Q_YK}=a_K^{-1}\circ Q_Y(\eta^C_K)$ and $\varepsilon^D_{Q_XL}=Q_X(\varepsilon^C_L)\circ b_L$. Their inverses lift by the same part, and the lifted composites are identities because lifting respects composition. For the first triangle, substitution of these formulas and naturality of $p,q,\varepsilon^D$ give
$$
p_K\circ\bigl(\varepsilon^D_{F_DQ_YK}\circ F_D(\eta^D_{Q_YK})\bigr)\circ p_K^{-1}
=Q_X\bigl(\varepsilon^C_{C(F)K}\circ C(F)(\eta^C_K)\bigr)=\mathrm{id}.
$$
For the second triangle, substitution and naturality of $p,q,\eta^D$ give
$$
q_L\circ\bigl(G_D(\varepsilon^D_{Q_XL})\circ\eta^D_{G_DQ_XL}\bigr)\circ q_L^{-1}
=Q_Y\bigl(C(G)(\varepsilon^C_L)\circ\eta^C_{C(G)L}\bigr)=\mathrm{id}.
$$
The final equalities are the degreewise triangle identities. Cancelling $p_K,q_L$ proves the triangles after precomposition with $Q_Y,Q_X$, respectively; part (3) of the localization node therefore proves the two triangle identities on the derived categories. Thus these are a unit and counit for an equivalence with functor $F_D$ and inverse $G_D$.

proof.text: Here is the fully faithful and essentially surjective conclusion explicitly. For $K,L\in D(\mathcal A)$ and $v:F_DK\to F_DL$, set $u=(\eta^D_L)^{-1}\circ G_D(v)\circ\eta^D_K$. Naturality of $\varepsilon^D$ and the triangle identity $\varepsilon^D_{F_DK}\circ F_D(\eta^D_K)=\mathrm{id}$ give $F_D(u)=v$. Conversely, for $u:K\to L$, naturality of $\eta^D$ gives $(\eta^D_L)^{-1}\circ G_D(F_D(u))\circ\eta^D_K=u$, so this is a two-sided inverse to the map on Hom sets. For every $M\in D(\mathcal B)$, the component $\varepsilon^D_M:F_DG_DM\xrightarrow{\sim}M$ supplies a preimage up to isomorphism. Consequently $Lg^*\cong F_D$ is fully faithful and essentially surjective.

proof.text: Finally let $h:Y\to X$ be the inverse scheme isomorphism. The direct-image formula of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] gives $(G\mathcal M)(V\xrightarrow{v}Y)=\mathcal M(X\times_YV\to X)$. The fibre product here is canonically the object $(V\xrightarrow{h\circ v}X)$: its map to $X\times_YV$ is $(h\circ v,\mathrm{id}_V)$ and its inverse is the projection to $V$; the two inverse identities follow from $gh=\mathrm{id}_Y$ and $hg=\mathrm{id}_X$. Part (1) of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image], applied to $h$, therefore identifies $G$ with $h^{-1}$, naturally in $V$ and $\mathcal M$. Part (3), applied to $h$, identifies the constant coefficient rings. Under the fibre-product identification, the two coefficient maps from $A_Y$ to $GA_X$ agree: their composites with the constant presheaf send every $a\in A$ to the same constant section $a$, so the defining uniqueness of $\rho^g_A$ in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] makes them equal as sheaf maps. Thus for every object $V$ and every $s\in A_Y(V)$, the two $A_Y(V)$-actions are restriction along this same coefficient map; the comparison on module sections commutes with that action because the fibre-product comparison acts by a module-sheaf restriction isomorphism. This proves an isomorphism of module functors, naturally on objects and morphisms. Apply it degreewise and descend the resulting natural isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](2). The finite-level clause of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], now applied to $h$, identifies the resulting termwise functor with $Lh^*$. Hence the quasi-inverse $G_D$ constructed above is termwise $g_*$ and is naturally isomorphic to $L(g^{-1})^*$, as asserted.
